verses.text: The men of Israel had made a promise at Mizpah: "None of us will give his daughter in marriage to a man from Benjamin."
The people went to Bethel, where they sat before God until evening, crying loudly and bitterly.
"LORD, God of Israel," they cried, "why has this happened to Israel? Why is one tribe missing from Israel today?"
Early the next day the people built an altar there and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

Then the Israelites asked, "Who from all the tribes of Israel did not come to the gathering before the LORD?" They had made a solemn promise that anyone who did not come to the LORD at Mizpah must be put to death.
The Israelites felt sorry for their relatives, the people of Benjamin. "Today one tribe has been cut off from Israel," they said.
"How can we find wives for those who are left, since we have promised by the LORD not to give them any of our daughters in marriage?"
Then they asked, "Which one of the tribes of Israel did not come to the LORD at Mizpah?" They found that no one from Jabesh Gilead had come to the camp for the gathering.
When they counted the people, they found that none of the people of Jabesh Gilead were there.
So the community sent twelve thousand of their best fighting men with orders to go to Jabesh Gilead and kill everyone living there with the sword, including the women and children.
"This is what you must do," they said. "Kill every male and every woman who has slept with a man."
Among the people living in Jabesh Gilead they found four hundred young women who had never slept with a man, and they took them to the camp at Shiloh in Canaan.
Then the whole community sent a message of peace to the people of Benjamin at the rock of Rimmon.
So the men of Benjamin came back at that time and were given the women of Jabesh Gilead who had been spared. But there were not enough for all of them.
The people felt sorry for Benjamin, because the LORD had made a gap in the tribes of Israel.
The elders of the community said, "The women of Benjamin have been killed. How can we find wives for the men who are left?
The survivors of Benjamin must have heirs," they said, "so that a tribe of Israel will not be wiped out.
But we cannot give them our daughters as wives, since we Israelites have promised, 'Cursed is anyone who gives a wife to a man from Benjamin.'
But look, there is the yearly festival of the LORD at Shiloh, north of Bethel, east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah."
So they told the men of Benjamin, "Go and hide in the vineyards
and watch. When the young women of Shiloh come out to dance, rush out of the vineyards. Each of you catch a wife from the women of Shiloh and go home to the land of Benjamin.

When their fathers or brothers come to complain to us, we will say, 'Please be kind to them for our sake. We did not get wives for them in the war, and you did not give your daughters to them, so you are not guilty of breaking your promise.'"

So that is what the men of Benjamin did. Each man caught one of the young women as they were dancing and carried her off to be his wife. Then they went back to their own land, rebuilt their towns and settled in them.
At that time the Israelites left that place and went home to their own tribes and clans, each to their own land.
In those days Israel had no king. Everyone did whatever they thought was right.
